items.body: Utah defeats Colorado in chippy game that features big hits, multiple fights SALT LAKE CITY -- If the Utah Mammoth and Colorado Avalanche play outdoors New Year’s Eve the way they did indoors Wednesday, it won’t just be chilly. It’ll be chippy. Utah won 4-1 at Delta Center in an intense, physical game that Mammoth coach Andre Tourigny hopes is a preview of the Discover NHL Winter Classic . “That would be pretty good, eh?” Tourigny said with a smile. “Honestly, what you want more than that? Great fights. Great hits. The bodychecks were flying. The two teams did not like each other, were going at each other, played the right way, played hard. That’s a good night for hockey.” When Utah joined the NHL in 2024-25, one of the questions was which team would become its rival. Colorado seemed logical, if only because the two teams shared geography, topography and the Central Division. Colorado-Utah wasn’t much of a rivalry the past two seasons. The Avalanche went 5-1-1 against the Mammoth, including 3-0-1 at Delta Center. The teams had no history of animosity. But Colorado was selected as Utah’s opponent for the Winter Classic, and then came Wednesday. The NHL and Fanatics unveiled the Winter Classic jerseys in the morning, and many fans wore them at Delta Center. The game was on national television. items.title: Mammoth beat Avalanche to end six-game slide
items.body: SALT LAKE CITY — Vincent Trocheck scored a goal and assisted another to help the Utah Mammoth beat the Colorado Avalanche 4-1 on Wednesday night and snap a six-game losing streak. Liam O’Brien, Dmitri Simashev and Kevin Stenlund scored goals for the Mammoth. Sebastian Cossa made 30 stops. Mackenzie Blackwood tallied 25 saves for Colorado. Jaden Schwartz scored the lone goal for the Avalanche. O’Brien put Utah on the board at 5:22 of the second, blasting a one-timer from the faceoff circle for his first goal of the season. Trocheck made it a two-goal lead with a power-play goal with 2:07 left in the second. He slid out to the circle and slapped the puck home off a crisp feed from Keller. Utah went up 3-0 only 62 seconds into the third after Simashev snapped in the puck from the circle for a short-handed goal. Colorado started both the second and third periods with power-play chances but were unable to capitalize. Schwartz’s unassisted goal with 4:59 left helped the Avalanche avoid a shutout. Stenlund capped the scoring on an empty netter with 2:08 remaining.

items.title: Canadiens restore balance in bounce-back win over Devils
items.summary: After looking uncharacteristically sloppy on Monday, the Canadiens looked more like the team we’ve seen for most of their season with a win against the Devils.
items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Hours before the Montreal Canadiens bounced back from what Martin St. Louis termed to be “pretty much the worst” game they’d played this season, the coach sung his most common refrain. “All team sports are the same,” St. Louis began. “I didn’t invent these rules of being in space and breaking pressure with being in balance on the ice. When you play inside that, you raise your percentages of having success and you get the bounces. When you don’t do that, your percentages of having success go down and you go looking for bounces. When you do things the right way, you get goals and bounces and a high percentage of success.” That was what he said at his morning media availability. It was also the same message he delivered to his team right before it — guiding them through video of how they were out of balance in Monday’s 3-1 loss to the New York Rangers, explaining how they didn’t present the proper options to each other without the puck and therefore forced plays with it, and emphasizing that if they just returned to applying the basic principles of team sports against the New Jersey Devils, it would ensure Monday’s game was a one-off. Then St. Louis shuffled one player on each of his four lines and two of his three defence pairings, and the Canadiens went out and proved to themselves that if they play the way they’re supposed to, it doesn’t matter who they're on the ice with. items.title: Senators’ Tyler Boucher to have father Brian Boucher call game vs. Flyers
items.body: Ottawa Senators rookie Tyler Boucher will have a friendly face calling his game for the opposition broadcast on Thursday. His dad, former NHLer Brian Boucher, will be in the booth for NBC Philadelphia's local broadcast when the Philadelphia Flyers visit the Senators on Thursday — a game in which the younger Boucher is expected to play. "I mean, I'm going to try to keep it as normal as possible, treat him like another player, but I am going to be keeping a close eye on him for sure," Brian told NHL.com's Dan Rosen on Wednesday. "I've got to be honest with you, I've dreamt about this moment since he's been drafted. For me personally, I don't know about for him, but since I got into this side of the game I've always been like, 'Man, it would be so cool to call his games.' It would be really meaningful to me. I've never told him that because I've never wanted to put pressure on him, but for me personally it's going to be a special moment and I'm looking forward to it if it does happen." Brian played for the Flyers for six seasons in three separate stints before his retirement following the 2012-13 season. Tyler was selected by the Senators with the 10th-overall pick of the 2021 draft and made his debut on Tuesday night — scoring his first NHL goal in the process. The elder Boucher said that while he doesn't consider himself to be a typical hockey dad, he admitted that it's "better to be upstairs so (Tyler) doesn't see my facial reactions." "So, I'll be upstairs and he won't see my reactions if he makes a boneheaded play or something like that."

items.title: Canadiens end power-play drought in win, hand Hellebuyck 1st Devils loss
items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Jake Evans scored the go-ahead goal, captain Nick Suzuki ended his team's long power-play drought and the Montreal Canadiens defeated the New Jersey Devils 3-2 on Wednesday night to halt a two-game skid. Connor Hellebuyck got a piece of Evans' shot with his glove but could not keep it out of the net. The goal with 13:43 left sparked “Go, Habs, go!” chants from the many Canadiens fans in attendance. Hellebuyck allowed three goals on 27 shots and lost for the first time in eight starts since joining New Jersey in a trade from Winnipeg in late October. Despite Timo Meier setting up a goal by Luke Evangelista and scoring on a breakaway fresh out of the penalty box, the Devils had their two-game winning streak snapped, losing for just the second time in their past nine. The Canadiens only trailed for 40 seconds after Evangelista's goal, as Alex Newhook got in on net and made a nifty move to beat Hellebuyck and tie it. After spending time practicing the power play on Tuesday and devoting significant conversation to what was going wrong, they came up empty on their first two chances. With Montreal's run at 0 for its past 14, a parade to the penalty box eventually came back to bite New Jersey. Suzuki drew a tripping penalty on Brenden Dillon, then deflected Lane Hutson's point shot in past Hellebuyck with 41.9 seconds remaining in the first period. Jacob Fowler stopped all 20 shots he faced in the second and third, finishing with 27 saves and avoiding what would have been his first time losing consecutive games this season. He and his teammates successfully killed a penalty in the final minutes to seal it. items.title: Bruins beat Red Wings, spoil Detroit’s Centennial celebration game
items.body: DETROIT — David Pastrnak had a goal and an assist as the Boston Bruins beat Detroit 4-1 on Wednesday night and spoiled the Red Wings' Centennial celebration game. The contest was played on the 100th anniversary of Detroit’s first NHL game — a 2-0 loss for the then-Cougars to the Bruins. Pregame ceremonies on Wednesday included a video introduction from Scotty Bowman. The centennial celebration resulted in a rare color-on-color game, with Detroit wearing red and the Bruins in black. JJ Peterka and Pavel Zacha also scored for the Bruins, who snapped a three-game skid. Mason Lohrei and Morgan Geekie each had two assists. Daniil Tarasov, coming off a shutout of the Tampa Bay Lightning, made 27 saves, but couldn’t prevent Detroit’s sixth loss in seven games. Detroit's Lucas Raymond made it 1-0 at 16:58 of the first period. Keegan Kolesar knocked the puck loose in the neutral zone to set up a 2-on-1 break, and Raymond blasted Andrew Copp’s pass inside the left post for his ninth goal. Peterka tied the game at 2:47 of the second, cutting in from the left wing and beating Tarasov on the glove side. Zacha then gave the Bruins a 2-1 lead with a power-play goal at 11:48, putting in a rebound for his sixth of the season. Pastrnak made it 3-1 at 5:11 of the third, beating Tarasov from the slot after a pass from Lohrei. Casey Middelstadt finished the scoring into an empty net at 19:05.

items.body: Register Login Evening Notes: Maple Leafs, Bolduc, Shepard By Bradley Keith | at November 18, 2026 9:29 pm Unable to end what is now a brutal seven game losing streak after last night’s 6-3 loss to Chicago, the noise only gets louder for the Maple Leafs. David Pagnotta of The Fourth Period reports that President and CEO Keith Pelley traveled with the group for the game and had unpleasant conversations with what the insider called “key personnel” on the team. Not confirming exactly who it may have been, one can assume new head coach Jim Hiller ’s rough start to his tenure was a key part of any conversation. Even if the near-sighted decisions by John Chayka to make large commitments to an aging Sergei Bobrovsky , a late-blooming Darren Raddysh , and bottom-sixers like Colton Sissons would bite them sometime later, the expectation was at least to buy another 2-3 year window and figure out the rest in the future. Instead we’re not even in December and there’s already questions being raised . Toronto is 1-9-0 in their last 10, 27th in the NHL. Their offensive production has been acceptable, but it’s their other classic shortcomings which continue to hamper the group. Nearly two years ago today the Blues fired Drew Bannister 22 games into their season, although the coach had 76 total games behind the bench before the decision was made, counting the season prior. Considering everything at stake, one can’t rule out an abrupt change behind the bench sometime later this season before it is too late. Until that is a real possibility, Toronto will be desperate to get back into the win column tomorrow night against Hiller’s former Kings team.

items.body: The injury bug seems to keep on biting the Montreal Canadiens . Forward Zachary Bolduc exited Wednesday's game against the New Jersey Devils after suffering an apparent injury, the team told Sportsnet's Eric Engels . According to Engels, Bolduc was being evaluated by the team's medical personnel in the third period but provided no additional information as to the nature of his injury. It's unclear how Bolduc suffered the injury, but he exited in the second period and did not return to the team's bench to start the third. Bolduc played 12:34 of ice time before exiting and ended his night without a point, but tallied a shot on goal and a hit. The 23-year-old Trois-Rivières native has six goals and three assists in 21 games this season — his second campaign in Montreal.

The Columbus Blue Jackets raised a ceremonial banner to honor him, but have yet to officially retire the number. Nobody else has worn the #13 since his 181 games for the Jackets, however, and it’s safe to assume nobody will. Veteran Charlie Coyle has #3 on his sweater instead, since his arrival to the team having spent many years wearing the number previously. Having set deeper roots in Alberta across his nine years as a Flame, where Gaudreau’s 609 points rank sixth-best in franchise history, Calgary has yet to announce any intention to retire the number of their star who departed in free agency although no player has worn the number after him either. Given the circumstances of how the spectacular talent’s career was tragically cut short before his 12th NHL season, it would typically be customary for Boston College to pay tribute in such a way. To ramp him back up to playing speed, the Islanders have also assigned Ritchie to the Hamilton Hammers in the AHL. A few days later, the Islanders announced that Ritchie would miss four to six weeks. Before the injury, Ritchie struggled to produce, registering a goal and an assist in eight games with a net-zero rating, averaging 12:11 of ice time per game. Despite the relatively low offensive production, Ritchie hovered around the middle of the pack on the team in CorsiFor and on-ice SV%. Once he suits up for the Hammers, it’ll be Ritchie’s first AHL appearance of the 2026-27 campaign. He played three AHL contests last season with the Bridgeport Islanders, scoring one goal and three points. Still, he spent the majority of the season with the Islanders, finishing with 13 goals and 30 points in 65 games with a -14 rating, averaging 13:28 of ice time. It was his first season with New York. Before his time with the Islanders, Ritchie was with the Colorado Avalanche. The former 27th overall pick of the 2023 NHL Draft began the 2024-25 campaign with the Avalanche, scoring one goal in seven games with a -7 rating. items.body: Former goalie will broadcast forward’s next game against Flyers on Thursday The 49-year-old former NHL goalie has spent his entire life in the game, more than half of it in the League as either a player or broadcaster, but never before did he experience what he felt while in the stands at Canada Life Centre in Winnipeg alongside his wife, Melissa, and daughter, Brianna, watching his son, Tyler, score the game-winning goal in his NHL debut with the Ottawa Senators. "I mean, I've had some cool moments in my career; five shutouts in a row stands out," said Boucher, who set the NHL record for longest shutout streak (332:01) in 2003-04. "Win an eight-period game in Pittsburgh in the playoffs, five overtimes (in 2000). But this is better just because it's your kid, and we're all so proud of our children." Tyler Boucher was selected by the Senators with the No. 10 pick in the 2021 NHL Draft, but injuries and four surgeries, two on his knee and one on each shoulder, derailed the 23-year-old's journey to the NHL until he finally got there and scored at 4:04 of the second period to give Ottawa a two-goal lead en route to a 2-1 win. "I think what I'm most proud of with him, honestly, it's not that he played his first NHL game or that he scored, that's awesome stuff, but it's the story behind it and the resilience and perseverance and fight that he showed," Brian Boucher said. "He really dug in. I mean, he's had nothing but setbacks and disappointments for five years since being drafted. I'm sure he questioned, and I know I did deep down inside, would this day ever come. To play in the NHL, it's a privilege, it's not a right, and I'm so happy he was able to fulfill his dream of getting that game and scoring. items.title: Former NHLer Craig Anderson says his game slipped following release of GTA 5
items.summary: GTA 6, the next installment in the popular video game franchise, is set to be released on Thursday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Marc DesRosiers-USA TODAY Sports Grand Theft Auto IV (GTA 6), the long-awaited next installment in the ultra-popular video game franchise, is finally set to be released on Thursday. While you wouldn’t think the release of a new video game would have any effect on an NHL season, former NHL goaltender Craig Anderson is here to tell you otherwise. On Wednesday’s episode of the Absolute Non-Sens podcast, Anderson revealed that the release of GTA 5 directly led to a drop-off in his play back in 2013 while with the Ottawa Senators . “My worst season that I felt I had in Ottawa, was the year that ‘Grand Theft Auto V’ came out,” Anderson said. “Direct correlation. Just a time suck. You’d play after a game, you’d get home 11-11:30, you’d start playing that game and it’d be 4 AM and you’d be like ‘I’m not even tired’. Now Grand Theft Auto VI is coming out so it’ll be interesting to see how that all plays out.” While the 2013-14 season wasn’t actually Anderson’s worst with the Senators, as his play tailed off pretty dramatically in his age-36 season of 2017-18, his numbers that year do stand out as noticeably worse than those from the seasons surrounding it, lending credence to his GTA 5 theory. In the 2012-13 season, the Park Ridge, Illinois native led the league with a .941 save percentage and a 1.68 goals-against average, finishing fourth in voting for the Vezina Trophy. In 2013-14, he dipped to a .911 SV% and a 3.00 GAA, before bouncing back to a .923 SV% and a 2.49 GAA in 2014-15. items.title: Reeling Penguins at crossroads as ‘Big Three’ era winds down
items.summary: It took Kyle Dubas more than three years, but the Pittsburgh Penguins general manager finally said the quiet part out loud.
items.body: CRANBERRY TOWNSHIP, Pa. — It took Kyle Dubas more than three years, but the Pittsburgh Penguins general manager finally said the quiet part out loud. Asked Wednesday what gives him hope that his struggling team, which is mired near the bottom of the Eastern Conference and has three regulation wins through 20 games, can turn it around in time to salvage this season, Dubas turned philosophical. Yes, making the playoffs for a second straight year would be nice. Yet that's not the metric he will lean on to gauge progress. Dubas would like the team's younger players to take “major steps.” He'd like to see the iconic, aging core led by captain Sidney Crosby show it still has “gas left in the tank." He'd like some of the prospects he's acquired since taking over to make a push for NHL playing time. If those things can happen, Dubas believes the franchise will be on “the right track" regardless of where the Penguins wind up in the standings. Then, Dubas finished by using a phrase that included the one word he has consistently avoided uttering publicly since taking over in the summer of 2023. “This has been, I think rightfully, an unorthodox style of rebuilding a team because of the players that are here,” he said. items.title: Things we (think we) know: Oilers forging different identity under Babcock
items.summary: The Oilers are becoming a different team under Mike Babcock. They’re finding ways to win beyond McDavid and Draisaitl, playing a more complete brand of hockey, and closing the gap on the NHL’s elite.
items.body: We’ve written a lot over the years about an Oilers team that needed to get “one win better” after the 2024 Final, or find “just a few more periods of winning hockey” after losing to Florida again in 2025. Of course, it doesn’t work quite that way. When you win six playoff series in two years, you’re obviously doing most things right. The Leafs have won just eight playoff rounds this century, Vancouver nine, Montreal 13, and Calgary five. Edmonton has been elite, but still, Florida had something that they did not. You can’t change out your entire roster, but you can change how your roster plays. That’s what Mike Babcock is in the process of doing these days. The same players, mostly, are playing a different brand of hockey. And if there is one surprise in Edmonton, it’s that almost all of them are succeeding at the transition. That Babcock separated Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl for the first time all season Tuesday in Sunrise, and Edmonton scored four goals plus an empty-netter, is bad news for the rest of hockey. For one night at least, it wasn’t entirely the McDavid, Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard show. The Oilers beat Florida with two scoring lines, the best power play in hockey, depth players who won their shifts, a perfect penalty kill and better goaltending than Jacob Markstrom gave the Panthers. Sure, Florida was missing Sasha Barkov and Brad Machand), and tired after a long run of games. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: PWHL I guess there is a new Captain Clutch… On Wednesday, the Detroit Clutch announced that forward Hilary Knight has been named the franchise’s first captain. The expansion team also announced that forwards Daryl Watts and Jesse Compher will serve as alternates for the franchise’s inaugural season. Watts and Compher were both signed by the Clutch during Phase 2 of the PWHL Expansion Player Distribution Process , with Watts signing a league-record four-year contract. Knight initially signed with the Vegas Vanguards , but was traded to Detroit once the move could be made official prior to the 2026 PWHL Draft . She’s had some success in the young league, earning a share of the Points Leader Award with New York Sirens forward Sarah Fillier in 2024-25. Fans will have the opportunity to bid on the jersey during the annual broadcast auction, with benefits supporting the Minnesota Wild Foundation. Back here on Earth, the Wild debuted their Hometown Remix jerseys in a 7-3 win against the Nashville Predators on Tuesday. The jerseys will see the ice nine more times this season, the next time being against the Colorado Avalanche on Nov. 27 (4 p.m. ET; TVAS, Wild+, ALT, MINNHL).

The Pittsburgh Penguins know that. Crosby, in his 22nd NHL season, has seemingly never had an expiration date. That remains true to the Penguins, the only team the 39-year-old center has played for since being selected No. 1 in the 2005 NHL Draft. However, for the first time, Pittsburgh faces the reality there will come a time when Crosby is simply not around. That might not be immediately true, even with the Penguins captain in the final season of a two-year, $17.4 million contract ($8.7 million average annual value). But it will be one day, and Pittsburgh could trade valuable veterans to be prepared. "I think it becomes more realistic when you lose some games, and that's the unfortunate part of losing," Crosby said Wednesday. "I've always said that losing itself isn't fun, but it's everything that comes with it. It's trades. It's a lot of things. And the finger gets pointed a lot of different ways. "Unfortunately, that's the way it goes. That's the difference between winning and losing." After defying expectations last season and finishing second in the Metropolitan Division (41-25-16) to return to the Stanley Cup Playoffs following three straight misses, the Penguins (7-11-2) have stumbled out of the gate. items.body: Pittsburgh Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas doesn't seem eager to give up valuable assets in order to improve his team's position in the Metropolitan Division. Speaking during his quarter-mark-of-the-season news conference , Dubas acknowledged that he has seen flashes of the team he wants Pittsburgh to become, but the consistency hasn't been there. The Penguins sit seventh in the Metropolitan Division and the organization is in a position where it has to decide whether to make additions to a veteran roster or continue prioritizing its long-term plans. Dubas didn't hesitate to make his position clear on moving out future assets this season to remain competitive. “No, we wouldn’t,” Dubas said. “I don't think it's prudent for the Pittsburgh Penguins to give up future draft picks or prospects to add more veterans to our group.” While Dubas isn't ruling out making trades, the Penguins are more likely to explore opportunities involving younger players who could benefit from a change of scenery. One example Dubas pointed to from last season was trading for Egor Chinakhov. items.body: The Utah Mammoth and Colorado Avalanche are set to sport some new threads. The National Hockey League unveiled the uniforms each team will wear for the upcoming Winter Classic on Wednesday. The outdoor game will take place at Rice-Eccles Stadium on the University of Utah campus in Salt Lake City on New Year's Eve. It marks Utah's first outdoor game and the first played by the Mammoth, the lone franchise that hasn't played one yet. It also marks the 47th regular-season outdoor game all-time. The uniforms are designed by Fanatics, the NHL's official outfitter, and are heavily inspired by the ski culture shared by Utah and Colorado. The Mammoth are set to wear a light-blue jersey with brown and beige detailing, featuring a woolly mammoth on the crest. Meanwhile, the Avalanche uniforms are burgundy, navy and beige, drawing on jersey designs from the franchise's past, with the front crest featuring a 'C' with mountains inside. items.body: The Maple Leafs rookie selected No. 1 overall at the 2026 draft stepped on the ice for his solo lap at the start of warm-ups — a playful, often helmetless indoctrination for players set to make their debuts — in late September. Toronto goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky was so in the zone ahead of the season-opener that he mistakenly joined the 18-year-old before later apologizing for the gaffe. McKenna wasn't fussed. Like every other youngster taking that solitary twirl, he was living out a childhood dream. "Hard to forget a day like this," the peach-fuzzed winger said. "All pretty special." The league's rookie lap is a relatively new tradition, one started organically when veterans began hiding helmets ahead of first games — a prank that became ingrained in most teams' culture — before the rest of the roster joins warm-ups after a few dozen lonely strides around the rink. Logan Cooley came out of the tunnel on his own as a member of the Arizona Coyotes in New Jersey back in 2023. "I wish in the moment I could have enjoyed it a lot more," said Cooley, now a forward with the Utah Mammoth following the franchise's relocation. items.body: Designs for Avalanche, Mammoth inspired by outdoor hockey, alpine nostalgia NEW YORK – Today, the National Hockey League (NHL) and Fanatics, the authentic outfitter of the NHL, unveiled uniforms for the Discover NHL Winter Classic, to be worn when the Utah Mammoth host the Colorado Avalanche on New Year’s Eve at Rice-Eccles Stadium on the campus of the University of Utah in Salt Lake City. items.summary: ST. LOUIS -- Cutter Gauthier hears all the noise and sees all the headlines.
items.body: Forward closing in on Selanne after fourth hat trick of season in loss to Blues ST. LOUIS -- Cutter Gauthier hears all the noise and sees all the headlines. So, the Anaheim Ducks forward is doing his best to adopt tunnel vision as he continues to score goals at a record pace. That was evident again on Tuesday, when he extended his goal streak to 10 games by getting a hat trick, his fourth during the run, in an 8-6 loss to the St. Louis Blues at Enterprise Center. ANA@STL: Gauthier records his fourth hat trick of the season and fifth of his career The 22-year-old, who also had an assist in the loss, has 19 goals during the streak, which is one game shy of tying Teemu Selanne (Oct. 21 to Nov. 10, 1997) for the longest in Ducks history. He's also the third player in NHL history to have a goal streak of at least 10 games before the age of 23, joining Babe Dye (11 games in 1920-21) and Mike Bossy (10 games in 1978-79). "It obviously gets published a lot what’s going on, but if I let the online chats and stuff, the pressure and all that stuff, get to me, it’s not going to be good," Gauthier told NHL.com. "When I play at my best, I’m playing free. I’m not thinking, I’m just flowing, I’m using my instincts and being great. I don’t let that affect me. I haven’t these last handful of weeks, so I’m going to keep that going." Gauthier certainly hasn't let it affect him, considering he has 24 points (19 goals, five assists) during an NHL career-high 12-game point streak. He also has 21 goals in 21 games this season, which is tied with Leon Draisaitl of the Edmonton Oilers for the NHL lead. items.body: Forward to see time defending Suzuki, type of responsibility captain welcomes NEWARK, N.J. -- Nico Hischier knows his most important contribution for the New Jersey Devils won't always appear on the score sheet. That might be winning a defensive-zone face-off, staying above the puck instead of joining the rush or sacrificing an offensive opportunity to remain on the proper side of an opposing star. Those details will again be critical when the Devils host the Montreal Canadiens at Prudential Center for NHL on Prime "Wednesday Night Hockey" (7:30 p.m. ET; MSGSN, Prime). The Devils captain likely will spend significant time against Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki , who has 17 points (eight goals, nine assists) in 15 games while winning 55.4 percent of his face-offs. Suzuki's intelligence, patience with the puck and chemistry with Cole Caufield , who leads Montreal with 12 goals in 21 games, will test Hischier's positioning and awareness. "I view it as part of my game I want to play, and I take that as my job that game, and it contributes to the team," Hischier said. "I obviously take pride in that. If you're able to shut down a good line, then you give your team a chance to win a hockey game." Those assignments, combined with Hischier's production on offense and leadership as captain, have earned him respect throughout the NHL and inside New Jersey's dressing room. The New York Islanders’ defenseman scored a hat trick during the team’s 5-1 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets Tuesday night, becoming the third teenage defenseman in NHL history to record three goals in a game. The other two teenage defenders to achieve the feat were Phil Housley and Hannu Virta, both with the Buffalo Sabres during the 1982-83 season. The Hamilton, Ont., native has 32 goals and 51 assists for 83 points in 102 career NHL contests. Schaefer is coming off one of the most impressive seasons for a rookie defenseman in NHL history. He finished with 23 goals and 36 assists for 59 points, averaged 24:41 of ice time per game, capped off by winning the 2026 Calder Trophy for rookie of the year . His 23 goals placed him second among all NHL defenseman in 2025-26, behind only Jakob Chychrun of the Washington Capitals . He made NHL history by tying Hockey Hall of Famer Brian Leetch for the most goals by a rookie defender , and also became the youngest blueliner in NHL history to reach 50 points in a season . Schaefer was selected by the Islanders with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NHL Entry Draft, despite the fact he played just 73 career OHL regular-season games due to injuries. Bedard gave Chicago the lead for good on his seventh goal with 1:19 left in the second period, which made it 3-2. Chicago's Spencer Knight stopped 31 shots and defenceman Sam Rinzel finished with three assists. The Blackhawks entered with the NHL’s third-worst power play at 14.3% but went 2 for 3 with the man advantage. Chicago has five power-play goals in its last eight attempts. After a scoreless first period, Batherson recorded his 11th goal of the season at 3:06 of the second and Boucher's goal followed 58 seconds later. Boucher, 23, was selected 10th overall in the 2021 NHL draft, but battled with injuries for a number of seasons. He was recalled from the AHL Belleville Senators on Sunday. Bjorck was Winnipeg's first-round pick (eighth overall) in this year's draft. Jets: Fans chanted “Viggo, Viggo” after the 18-year-old Swede scored his first NHL goal in his 22nd game. items.summary: Defenceman Matthew Schaefer recorded his first NHL hat trick and Anthony Duclair had a goal and an assist as the New York Islanders beat the Columbus Blue Jackets 5-1 on Tuesday night.
items.body: NEW YORK — Defenceman Matthew Schaefer recorded his first NHL hat trick and Anthony Duclair had a goal and an assist as the New York Islanders beat the Columbus Blue Jackets 5-1 on Tuesday night. Schaefer became the second-youngest defenseman in NHL history to record a hat trick. Only Hall of Famer Phil Housley at 18 years, 320 days was younger than Schaefer at 19 years, 73 days. Schaefer joined Housley as the only players at the position to reach 30 goals before age 20. The 19-year-old Schaefer opened his scoring 1:34 into the second period. He scored twice in the third, at 7:01 off assists from Duclair and Ryan Pulock, and capped his night by scoring his ninth goal of the season into an empty net with 3:52 remaining. Schaefer’s hat trick is the first by an Islanders defenceman since Denis Potvin in 1982. Anthony DeAngelo also scored for the Islanders, who won their third straight game after a four-game skid. Ilya Sorokin finished with 28 saves. Zach Werenski spoiled Sorokin's bid for a shutout with a goal 1:12 into the third period. items.title: Blackhawks’ Connor Bedard exits vs. Maple Leafs with apparent injury
items.body: The Chicago Blackhawks captain could be staring down another injury. Connor Bedard exited Tuesday's game against the Toronto Maple Leafs early in the third period after appearing to suffer an injury off a face-off. Bedard appeared to be in immediate pain after the draw and headed off the ice and to the dressing room, favouring his right arm. He did not return to the game, which the Blackhawks won 6-3. After the game, head coach Jeff Blashill had no concrete update and said that Bedard will undergo more testing on Wednesday that will give the team a better idea on the extent of his injury. "It looked like what it looked like," Blashill told reporters . "I hate to comment further until I know more." The 21-year-old has a history of shoulder injuries, missing extended time last season with a right shoulder injury and undergoing surgery on his left shoulder in the off-season. Bedard missed the first five Blackhawks games of the season as he rehabbed the injury. Prior to exiting on Tuesday, Bedard scored Chicago's go-ahead goal. items.summary: Connor McDavid had a goal and an assist to extend his season-opening points streak to 23 games, and the Edmonton Oilers continued their sizzling start by beating the rival Florida Panthers 5-2 on Tuesday night.
items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Connor McDavid had a goal and an assist to extend his season-opening points streak to 23 games, and the Edmonton Oilers continued their sizzling start by beating the rival Florida Panthers 5-2 on Tuesday night. McDavid now has 13 goals and 42 assists, and the 23-game streak to start a season ties Wayne Gretzky for the fifth-longest in NHL history. Only Gretzky (51- and 30-game streaks), Quebec's Mats Sundin (30) and Pittsburgh's Mario Lemieux (28) had longer streaks to open a season. Vasily Podkolzin scored twice, while Kasperi Kapanen and Leon Draisaitl each had a goal and two assists for Edmonton, which lost the 2024 and 2025 Stanley Cup finals to Florida. Devon Levi got the win in net for the Oilers, improving to 10-1-0 on the season. Matthew Tkachuk scored twice in the third period for Florida, which trailed 4-0 entering the final minutes. It was his first multi-goal game of the season. Edmonton (17-3-3) won its sixth straight and has 37 points through 23 games, tying for the second-most in team history. The 55 points through 23 games have McDavid in elite company. Only two other players — Gretzky and Lemieux, both doing it on three occasions — have managed that many points this quickly into a season. Lemieux was the last to do it, posting 66 points through 23 games in 1995-96. The Panthers were again without forwards Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, who have both been sidelined for all but two games of the season. Panthers coach Paul Maurice said both are expected to meet with physicians later this week, an indicator that their returns to the lineup could be looming.

Along with a one-night-only exhibit featuring rare artifacts, historic memorabilia and photography in the atrium section of United Center, the Blackhawks had all five of their ambassadors take part in a Q&A about 90 minutes before the game: former forwards Eddie Olczyk , Denis Savard and Jeremy Roenick , former defenseman Chris Chelios and former play-by-play broadcaster Pat Foley. items.body: Mark Scheifele is well on his way to rewriting the Winnipeg Jets ' record books. Leading the comeback with a four-point effort and the shootout winner over the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday, Scheifele passed his mentor Dale Hawerchuk for most career points in franchise history with 933. The milestone carried some added weight, as the history-making coincided with the Jets' mentors trip. Shifting from the traditional "dad's trip," every player got to invite a male mentor on Winnipeg's two-game road swing through Dallas and Chicago. Scheifele, whose father, Brad, died of cancer in May 2025, invited Gregg Derlago, his billet dad during his early years in Winnipeg. Derlago had given Scheifele a pin with a picture of him and his dad when he was younger, which he wore after the game while being interviewed by reporters. "He's up there watching, and Dale's up there watching as well," Scheifele said. "Pretty special to do this tonight with all the mentors here. On Tuesday, the IIHF website was the victim of a cyberattack. As of 2 p.m. ET, IIHF.com is still down. items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google Alex Ovechkin’s third stop on his farewell tour lands in Tampa Bay, Fla., Tuesday night. Ahead of his final road game at Benchmark International Arena, the Washington Capitals captain was met by Lightning defensemen Victor Hedman and John Carlson , along with assistant coach Jeff Halpern . Hedman presented Ovechkin with a custom-made cigar box and cigars stamped with an image of the Russian winger’s famous “Hot Stick celebration.” View this post on Instagram “Well, we got this for you, Ovi,” Hedman said. “Obviously you’ve been terrorizing us for a long time, so we got you a personalized cigar box, and I don’t know if you can see what’s on the cigar?” “It’s the Hot Stick,” Hedman continued. “You did it in this building the year before I got here, so I didn’t see it live. We just want to congratulate you on an amazing career. It’s been an honor to play against you, so this is from us.” Ovechkin famously scored the 50th goal of his 2008-09 season on the road against the Lightning on March 19, 2009, and to celebrate laid his stick on the ice and pantomimed it being on fire with his gloves. “It was pretty funny,” Ovechkin said Tuesday . “Thanks for Tampa organization do that kind of gift for me. It’s special. I have guitar (from Nashville) and cigars, we’ll see what’s going next.” Ovechkin also reflected on then Hockey Night in Canada host Don Cherry’s emphatic panning of what he deemed to be showing up the Lightning. “Yeah, it was special moment, 50, and I tell the boys right away I’m going to do Hot Stick,” Ovechkin said. “I remember Don Cherry was not happy about it.
